questions.text: For the lease deed underlying the primary disputed tenancy, does the supplied record establish that the deed was UNREGISTERED? Registered is contrary evidence; a tenancy existing is not proof that a deed exists or is registered.

Does the supplied record establish a written permission by the landlord, specific to the primary disputed transfer/occupation and its recipient? All conditions must concern the same permission and disputed event. General associate-concern wording and permission by a tenant to family do not satisfy this condition.

Does the supplied record explicitly report a court finding that the tenant parted with possession in the primary disputed transfer? A named lower-court finding counts. A party allegation, eviction order alone, finding of subletting alone, or a precedent finding does not substitute for this precise finding.

answer_semantics.SUPPORTED: Complete witness meeting every required field and accepted source status.
answer_semantics.REFUTED: Explicit accepted contrary evidence resolving the primary target condition, not mere absence of a witness or failure of one candidate.
answer_semantics.UNKNOWN: No complete witness or decisive contrary evidence; include omitted/extraction-unknown fields and unadopted allegations.
answer_semantics.CONFLICT: Both accepted support and contrary evidence for the same object/event and compatible stage; statements from different cases are not a conflict.

source_scope: Complete unchanged V2 allowed appeal-input view, not full judgment. Current appeal reasoning/disposition stays excluded. Same scope for reference and A/B.
selection: All three existing development cases in preserved sample order; no selection by new reference results.
